chapter: Coming up in New York and Harlem theatres
title: Rehearsing shows at the Lafayette and his first arranging job
summary: After a Brooklyn employer fails to pay, he moves to rehearsing shows at the Lafayette Theatre, arranging a dancer's show in 1928, then for Ethel Waters.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Anything else you want to tell me about that. What happened around that era. How did you get into writing and meeting all these different guys.
Did you join this Clef Club you were telling me about.
How did you meet Lucky Roberts and all that.

I used to go up to Lucky's place, see, and listen to Lucky and everything and Lucky knew me so he asked me if I wanted a job and that's when I got it. But when Small's opened up, no, this is before Small. See, I had a band over there in Brooklyn and the guy owed me a week's salary and we opened up that Monday night and he said he was going to pay me and he didn't pay me, so I said well, it's no music. He said, no -- I said to the fellows, don't you play. He pay me, we play. If he don't don't. So I take all my music out and go back up and then I started rehearsing shows, up in the Lafayette Theatre, Lafayette Hall and I'm trying to think of that guy that danced. He had his wife and she was a singer and that's the first show I arranged for him at the Lafayette Theatre, that's in '28 and then I arranged for Ethel Waters. Earl Dancer had the group.
You weren't talking about Butterbeans and Susie.
Was it Brown or somebody and Brown.
Oh, this guy used to have a tall hat and a cane. I can never think of his name, but I arranged.
So that was your first orchestration job.
And I told the fellows play just what I got on there and I'll correct it.
Just what you put on the table.

Yeah, play what I got on the paper and I'll correct it later on, and I used to go through all that music and play it and I used to tell the fellows, learn to read music, sight music. Learn that sight music and I want to talk about music now.
